metadata.subject: Computer Networks
metadata.title: Follow a DNS Lookup
metadata.description: Resolve domain names through cache and DNS records to real server addresses.

learning_objectives: Explain why DNS maps names to IP addresses.
Distinguish a cache hit from a cache miss.
Trace lookup events and the resulting cache update.

mission.title: Trace real DNS behavior
mission.description: Predict the lookup, then reveal each model-generated event.

introduction.title: Names become addresses
introduction.content: People remember names such as learn.example. Networks use IP addresses. DNS finds the address that belongs to a domain name; it does not fetch the webpage.

worked_example.title: A cache miss
worked_example.content: Trace what happens when the requested name is not already remembered.

steps.explanation: The client checks its empty cache and gets a miss.
The client remembers the returned address.

worked_example.conclusion: A cache hit returns a remembered address; a miss requires a DNS query and can update the cache.

resolve-dns: The lookup followed the cache state and DNS records, then exposed the matching server.
A cached answer avoided a DNS query but still resolved the same name-to-address relationship.

challenge.title: DNS trace challenge
challenge.continue_message: Challenge complete. Keep exploring DNS consequences.

phases.title: Resolve the domain
phases.instruction: Predict cache behavior, address, server, and event order.
phases.feedback: Follow cache check, optional DNS query, result, and cache update in order.

items.content: A matching cache entry creates a hit and avoids DNS_QUERY.

phases.title: Cached lookup
phases.instruction: Predict and trace a cache hit.
phases.feedback: Start by comparing the query with cache keys.

guidance.start_message: Trace a cache miss without hints.

phases.title: Uncached lookup
phases.instruction: Predict the full query and cache-update sequence.
phases.feedback: A miss queries DNS before resolution.

phases.title: Resolve or reject
phases.instruction: Determine whether the domain resolves and trace why.
phases.feedback: NOT_FOUND follows a miss when no DNS record matches.

guidance.start_message: Interpret an unfamiliar cache and record set independently.

phases.title: Master the lookup
phases.instruction: Predict all four fields and verify the generated trace.
phases.feedback: Separate cached data from authoritative DNS records.

thinking.title: Predict a hidden DNS trace
thinking.instruction: Inspect the cache, records, and query. Predict the exact consequence before revealing it.
thinking.do_not_execute: Work through cache and DNS behavior mentally.

feedback.all_correct: You predicted the entire hidden DNS consequence.
feedback.incorrect: Compare each field with the model-generated trace.

quiz.question: What does DNS primarily return for a domain name?

discovery.title: DNS discovery
discovery.summary: DNS resolves names to addresses. A cache can answer immediately; otherwise a DNS query finds the record and may update the cache.

sections.title: WHAT?
sections.content: DNS maps human-friendly domain names to IP addresses.

sections.title: CACHE
sections.content: A cache stores earlier answers so some lookups avoid a new DNS query.

sections.title: NOT A WEB FETCH
sections.content: DNS finds an address; HTTP later requests a resource from a server.

sections.title: REMEMBER
sections.content: Check cache, query DNS on a miss, then resolve or report not found.

alternate_explanations.title: Think of contacts
alternate_explanations.content: DNS is like finding a saved phone number from a person's name; it finds where to contact, not the conversation itself.

alternate_explanations.title: Walk through a miss
alternate_explanations.content: No cache entry → query DNS → receive 203.0.113.20 → store it → use that address.

recall.title: Recall
recall.prompt: In your own words, what changes between a DNS cache hit and cache miss?
recall.model_answer: A hit returns a cached address; a miss queries DNS and can store the returned address for later.
